description: Given a Dagster job with conditional Out branching, a runtime-computed branch, or a DynamicOut fan-out, author the matching Orchestra YAML — mutually-exclusive condition: stages for branches and a matrix block for fan-out, never conflating the two.

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster job to Orchestra (see files/config_load_mode_branch.py). The `full_refresh` config flag decides at trigger time whether the backfill branch or the incremental branch runs — only one of the two ops actually executes per run. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline with a full_refresh boolean input, a stage conditioned on ${{ inputs.full_refresh == true }} running the backfill task, and a mutually-exclusive stage conditioned on the false case running the incremental task.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares an input for the branch decision
full_refresh is referenced both as an input and inside a condition expression
A condition references inputs.full_refresh (a trigger-time / config-driven branch, not a runtime OUTPUTS lookup)
Both branch stages carry a condition key
The two conditions are genuinely mutually exclusive (one tests full_refresh true, the other tests false/not-true) rather than both able to evaluate true, or both false, in the same run
run_backfill and run_incremental land as separate tasks under their respective conditioned stages, not merged into a single task with branching logic written inside its parameters

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster job to Orchestra (see files/runtime_row_count_branch.py). Whether orders get loaded or a no-data notice fires depends on a row count computed during the run, not on any config passed in at trigger time. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live queries, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline where the check_staging_orders logic becomes an upstream task with set_outputs: true, and two downstream stages condition on that task's OUTPUTS — one for the positive/has-rows case running load_orders, one for the complementary case running send_no_data_notice.

assertions.text: The upstream check is a task that sets outputs for downstream conditions to read
A condition references the upstream task's OUTPUTS via ORCHESTRA.PIPELINE_RUN_TASKS
Downstream stages are sequenced after the check via depends_on
The value surfaced by check_staging_orders (row count or a has-data flag) is a real value from the source logic, not an invented placeholder key unrelated to what the op actually computes

load_orders conditions on the positive/has-rows case and send_no_data_notice conditions on the true complementary case, correctly mirroring has_new_orders vs no_new_orders rather than both being gated on the same condition or one left unconditioned

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster job to Orchestra (see files/dynamic_fanout_with_alert.py). list_regions fans out sync_region across three regions in parallel, then check_sync_results decides whether to fire send_failure_alert. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline where the DynamicOut fan-out becomes a matrix block on the region-sync task group (not a condition), sequenced into a separate stage conditioned on the upstream failure-check output that runs send_failure_alert only when failures occurred.

assertions.text: The fan-out is modeled as a matrix block
All three region values from list_regions appear as matrix inputs
The failure-alert stage is sequenced after the fan-out stage via depends_on
The DynamicOut fan-out is kept as a matrix block and is not also force-fit into a condition: expression — only the has_failures/all_clean branch gets a condition
send_failure_alert's condition references the check_sync_results output rather than an invented always-true/always-false stand-in, so the alert genuinely only fires when a region failed
